rounds.text: Makers Laboratories Ltd is drastically under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally low EV/EBITDA of 5.23x compared to the sector benchmark of 19.18x [E11]. The underlying business fundamentals are surging past historical performance, highlighted by a trailing twelve month sales growth of 24% [E16] and an astounding profit growth of 37,500% [E19]. Operating margins have expanded dramatically, reaching 25% in September 2026 compared to 7% a year prior [E28], driven by a clear multi-quarter and multi-year upward trend [E29, E30]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with borrowings down to Rs 4 Cr and a very conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E34, E36, E48], while generating robust free cash flow of Rs 11 Cr alongside strong cash conversion of 1.75x [E31, E33]. Conceded: the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4] and the 3-year median return on equity is low at -2% [E25]. Yet, with fundamentals dramatically outpacing historical share price growth [E44] and a reverse DCF implying that the current price assumes negative earnings growth [E43], the market fails to price in this fundamental turnaround.

Despite recent operational improvements, the historical capital efficiency of Makers Laboratories Ltd raises serious questions about whether its current valuation is fully supported. The company's median return on equity over the last 3 years sits at -2.5% [E25], and its 5-year median ROE is similarly depressed at -1% [E24], with filed statements explicitly flagging a low 3-year average ROE of -2.05% [E52] and a current ROE of only 3.2% [E13]. Furthermore, shareholders are receiving zero return in cash, as the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4], a point reinforced by official filings noting that despite reporting repeated profits, the company is withholding payouts [E51]. The stock has also experienced a massive run-up, currently trading at 96% of its 52-week range [E5] following a 166% share price growth over the past year [E23] and carrying a P/E ratio of 24.7x [E1]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent margin expansion and profit growth, such as a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 37500% and an operating margin increase of 17 percentage points [E19, E27]. However, this explosive short-term turnaround rests against a backdrop of prolonged historical unprofitability and low capital returns, leaving little margin for error at a 24.7x P/E multiple [E1].

Conceded: historical median ROE metrics over 3 and 5 years show negative figures [E24, E25], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, dismissing the business on these stale return metrics ignores a powerful structural turnaround that is already generating exceptional cash and profitability [E59]. The bear's focus on historical unprofitability is countered by current operating margins reaching 25% in September 2026—an 18 percentage point expansion year-over-year—and a cash conversion ratio of 1.75x where profits are fully backed by ₹ 14 Cr in operating cash flow [E28, E31, E32]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with borrowings reduced to ₹ 4 Cr alongside a comfortable current ratio of 2.56x, proving that the balance sheet is exceptionally secure [E34, E35, E36, E48]. The elevated P/E of 24.7x is entirely justified by a reverse DCF indicating that the market currently prices in negative earnings growth of -1.9%, vastly underestimating a business delivering a 37,500% TTM profit growth surge and surging foundational strength [E1, E19, E43, E44].

Conceded: the company reduced its debt to ₹ 4 Cr and reports an operating cash flow of ₹ 14 Cr for March 2026 [E32, E36]. However, the bull's dismissal of historical return metrics as merely "stale" is contradicted by the filed statements showing a current low ROE of 3% last year, alongside 3-year and 5-year median ROE figures sitting at -2% and -1% respectively [E24, E25, E26]. While the bull points to recent margin expansions and cash conversion [E28, E31], the fundamental reality remains that the business pays a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E51]. Furthermore, relying on a reverse DCF and TTM profit growth spikes to justify a P/E of 24.7x ignores the company's longer-term 5-year share price growth of just 7% [E1, E21, E43]. Finally, the rules-based screen explicitly flags the low 3% ROE as a material bear risk while rating overall confidence in the current setup as low at 69 out of 100 [E53, E58].
